headline: Better credit lifts earnings year over year
summary_short: Zions earned $262M, or $1.78 per diluted share, in Q3 2026 versus $1.48 a year ago, with net charge-offs falling to 0.02% of loans.
summary_long: EPS was down from $3.05 in Q2, when net earnings were $452M. Net interest income was $684M, up 2%, while NIM was 3.23%. Pre-provision net revenue was $340M, down 1%. Loans were $62.5B, up 4%, and total deposits $77.9B, up 4%. The provision was an $8M benefit versus a $49M expense. Tangible book value per share rose 13% to $43.50. The Basis Multifamily Finance acquisition closed in July.
confidence_notes: PPNR, adjusted noninterest income and expense, and ROTCE are non-GAAP as defined by Zions. Net earnings y/y change computed from $262M vs $221M. The release does not explain why Q2 net earnings of $452M were higher; the q/q comparison is not used for deltas. NIM comparison base ('compared with 3.28%') is read as the prior-year quarter.

drivers.explanation: The CEO says earnings rose primarily on improved credit quality, with net loan charge-offs of $3M versus $56M a year ago.
Management expects its moderately asset-sensitive balance sheet to produce stronger net interest income as rates rise; short and medium rates began rising in the last month of the quarter.
A net credit valuation adjustment gain of $10 million, or $0.05 per share, on client-related swaps contributed.
